item.title: We’re introducing new ways for Personal Intelligence and our best image generation model, Nano Banana 2, to generate images that reflect your life, i...
item.description:
We’re introducing new ways for Personal Intelligence and our best image generation model, Nano Banana 2, to generate images that reflect your life, interests, and the things you care about most.
Personal Intelligence securely connects the dots across Google apps like Google Photos and Gmail so Gemini can inherently understand your likes and interests. This allows you to skip long, complex prompts, so a simple request like "design my dream house" now automatically can reflect your unique style and taste. 🏡
Gemini can even use your labeled Google Photos library of you and your loved ones as a visual guide for your creations.
Try asking Gemini things like: “Create a claymation image of me and my family enjoying our favorite activity,” and watch your inner circle come to life, automatically.
You’re always in control: This remains an opt-in experience that you can adjust in your settings at any time.
It’s rolling out now for Google AI Plus, Pro, and Ultra subscribers in the U.S., and we plan to bring this to Gemini in Chrome desktops and more users soon.
Learn more → goo.gle/4cSDCDp

By analyzing hundreds of billions of signals, our AI models now better understand intent, helping us spot and block malicious content with incredible precision.
A few highlights from our 2025 Ads Safety Report: 🛡️ Gemini caught over 99% of policy-violating ads before they were ever served ⛔ Our teams blocked or removed over 8.3 billion bad ads 📉 And we reduced incorrect advertiser suspensions by 80%

item.title: The Gemini app is now available natively on Mac, bringing you a faster, more integrated way to get AI help right on your desktop. 🍎 With a quick ke...
item.description:
The Gemini app is now available natively on Mac, bringing you a faster, more integrated way to get AI help right on your desktop. 🍎
With a quick keyboard shortcut (Option + Space), you can bring up Gemini from anywhere on your screen, getting you the answers you need without switching tabs.
Here’s a few ways you can use it to streamline your work:
🖼️ Share your window: Get answers based on the documents, code, data or anything else you're looking at.
🎨 Stay in your creative flow: Quickly generate images with Nano Banana or videos with Veo without leaving your workspace.
💻 Quick access: Whether you’re drafting a report or building a complex spreadsheet, help is now just a keyboard shortcut away.
Available globally for users on macOS 15 and up at no cost. Download the Gemini app for Mac today → https://gemini.google/mac/

item.title: At our inaugural AI for the Economy Forum with MIT FutureTech, we brought together economists, industry leaders, policymakers and workforce training e...
item.description:
At our inaugural AI for the Economy Forum with MIT FutureTech, we brought together economists, industry leaders, policymakers and workforce training experts to discuss AI’s impact on jobs and the economy. We believe that by working together we can navigate the AI transition successfully. We also shared new investments focused on better understanding how AI will change the economy, training and apprenticeships:
-A new AI & Economy Research Program to answer pressing questions about AI's impact -New AI training for rural healthcare workers through a $10 million Google.org initiative in collaboration with the Johnson & Johnson Foundation  -$10 million in Google.org funding to support the Manufacturing Institute in its efforts to train U.S. workers in critical AI skills, and new apprenticeships for manufacturing employees as a pathway to new jobs -Expanded Google.org support for researchers exploring public policy solutions
Learn more about how we're working across sectors to get our economy AI-ready from James Manyika ⬇️Neither the benefits nor the risks of AI are automatic or guaranteed – a lot has to happen, things that we as a society must actively shape for the economic future we want.
That was the core premise of today’s AI for the Economy Forum in DC, co-hosted by Google and MIT FutureTech. Realizing AI’s full economic potential requires a new era of partnership across sectors, and we hope today was an important step toward building exactly that.
We were honored to be joined by leading economists, policymakers, and industry experts to tackle the most critical questions we face, including:  -What it will take to realize the economic potential from AI -New approaches to training and skill-building  -How AI will augment and change human expertise  -The research breakthroughs driving economic growth  -AI adoption and transformation needed in critical sectors like healthcare and education and manufacturing.
At Google we are deeply committed to shaping this transition positively and to benefit everyone. Today – in addition to investments we are already making in infrastructure, workforce, and education – we announced additional investments in research to better understand AI's economic shifts, alongside new workforce training initiatives
No single entity can navigate this shift alone. It will take all of us.
I left today's convening energized by the collaboration and important perspectives in the room. Enormous thanks to all the expert speakers.
Also on this World Quantum Day, it was a pleasure to discuss how advanced technologies’ – like AI and quantum computing – can drive economic growth with Under Secretary for Science at the Department of Energy Darío Gil and my colleague Charina Chou (COO of our Quantum AI team). So much important and exciting work ahead.
You can read more about the initiatives we announced today here: https://lnkd.in/gJxg3qRc
